classical_input: Gelfond-Schneider transcendence theorem, checked in the original logarithm formulation
author: A. Gelfond
title: Sur le septieme probleme de Hilbert
journal: Bulletin de l'Academie des Sciences de l'URSS, no. 4 (1934), 623-634
statement_checked: For nonzero algebraic numbers different from one, a ratio of their logarithms is rational or transcendental. The theorem and proof allow complex logarithms.
application: If z=exp(-pi alpha^2/S) were algebraic, log(z)/log(-1)=i alpha^2/S would be algebraic and nonrational for a positive integer alpha. This contradicts the cited theorem, so z is transcendental.
status: Classical theorem cited, not reproved or finitely certified. No floating exponential is evidence of transcendence.
